invariants: create records detached intent only; duplicate tracked/prepared/persisted IDs reject, including another cwd.
One storage cursor serializes the full batch and advances only after commit. Gaps, rewrites and lossy JSON reject. Missing IDs cannot be silently invented by append.
Cold append uses the same validated source/revision/repair commit as restore; live adoption retains open turns and verifies cwd/prefix. Retirement drops the owner cursor.
ensure_materialized flushes exact live state, persists an empty header once and invents no event.
Retired request/header-delta, mode/set and fallback headers reject writes. Unknown event types remain writable but reject on reads with artifact diagnostics.

Cold inspect/load validate current envelopes, message/request shape, header and surface rules via Session before durable repair. read_from remains a stored-prefix read and observes retirement/serialization/abort.
open_questions: Review rc.1 provider/consumer changes and obtain new acceptance; alpha observations cannot certify this revision.
identity: The session ID is shared by creation intent, cursor, reservation and exact live identity. Cwd is checked before live claims.
ownership: PersistenceCoordinator replaces the unused legacy queue facade. Backend methods own physical append/materialization; shared live/prepared layers own lifecycle and reservations.
ordering: Detach batch before awaiting the ID lock; validate cursor for the entire batch; commit header+first batch atomically; then advance cursor and invalidate cached source.
errors: First JSONL publication uses fsynced staging plus exclusive write-through MoveFileExW on Windows, or link/directory-fsync on POSIX. Missing Windows directories publish through the same write-through operation. Failed writes retain cursor and can retry.
cancellation: Queued read cancellation preserves the caller reason and does not cancel writers. Cold preparation cancellation retains its prior shared-work guarantees.
adaptation: Python 3.8 async methods snapshot when execution starts before waiting for the storage lock. ctypes calls the same Win7-compatible MoveFileExW API as upstream Windows publication. Two independent backend objects test exclusive publication, not arbitrary cross-process/multi-cwd coordination or power-loss behavior. Legacy native SQLite shares local compatibility tests only; canonical Source persistence acceptance uses JSONL none/zstd. Win7 machine validation remains deferred.

rc1_review.scope: The revised executable corpus and current Source inputs define bounded acceptance; historical alpha reviews remain historical.

historical_native_compatibility_notes: Any retained legacy native SQLite unit controls are product compatibility tests, not evidence for a canonical rc.1 SQLite persistence provider. Current Source persistence comparisons mount canonical JSONL none/zstd.
